correctness.rationale: On real BV of the unit circle, the Jordan derivative has equal positive/negative masses and admits a coupling into oriented arcs. The Hilbert triangle inequality reduces the full norm exactly to arcs with variation two. Arc Fourier energies give F_a''(L)=2[(K_a*K_a)(L)-2K_a(L)] away from zero; fourfold centered boxes produce F_a'(az)=p(z) and F_a(az)=a Phi(z) for 0<z<1 and all 0<a<=1/3. Strict convexity of p and p(0)=1>0>p(1)=-1/12 give a unique critical r. For a<L<=1/2, K_a=0, K_a*K_a>=0 and F_a'(1/2)=0, excluding additional maxima. The Fourier multiplier 1-sinc^2(pi k a) is strictly positive at all k!=0, so Hilbert equality rigidity yields exactly a single optimal arc. At a<=1/4 the separated-jump plateau is a/5, strictly smaller than a Phi(r). A standalone standard-library checker passes 1,628 exact-rational, decimal and bounded Fourier checks. No finite tests are substituted for continuum proof.

evidence: The unit-width centred order-two B-spline is the triangular convolution of two uniform box kernels. Costarelli-Vinti (2014), DOI 10.1216/JIE-2014-26-4-455, Section 6, use B-splines in discrete sampling Kantorovich approximation, not the residual of this circle convolution.

Mejía-Silvestre (2015), DOI 10.1155/2015/253636, define kth iterated forward Steklov averages in Lemma 7 and derive higher p-variation and fractional-modulus estimates. Those are not an exact full-Jordan-BV L2 residual norm.

originality.rationale: Inspected relevant full primary literature and searched the public index by object, function class, equivalent periodic B-spline representations, numerical root and sharp BV-L2 pulse patterns. Older articles address sampled Kantorovich schemes or kth p-variation Steklov estimates, while the present exact norm is for the centred convolution residual of order two. The distinct operator multipliers and sharp pulse length prevent implication from neighbouring boxcar or Poisson smoothing claims. No covering statement identified; indexing gaps and incomplete 2015 formula rendering leave acknowledged historical risk.
residual_risks: Public literature and indexed-record searches cannot exclude a pre-digital or unindexed exact inequality in another notation.
The 2015 full-text mirror has degraded equation glyphs; the high-level theorem scope is legible, but some low-level formulas may warrant later human comparison.
The result for wider bandwidths is deliberately unasserted; this is a scope limitation, not evidence of optimality beyond the stated range.

value.rationale: Iterated centered Steklov averaging is a natural positive B-spline smoother. Its exact BV-to-L2 error measures worst loss near edges for any bandwidth up to the geometrically natural one-third support threshold. The theorem gives a continuously parameterized sharp constant, identifies every extremal signal, and quantifies a nontrivial approximately 23.17 percent squared-error amplification from nearby opposite jumps compared with separated jumps; this is a meaningful interaction principle rather than routine reproduction or an arbitrary parameter slice.
